speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I need to understand the nature of your symptoms: Is your double vision constant or intermittent, and does the weakness in your upper limbs or difficulty climbing stairs affect just one side of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of binocular diplopia that worsens with up/down gaze, activity-induced proximal weakness, and complete recovery with rest is classic for this condition.
